executive.label: Attribution conclusion
executive.bottom_line: The portfolio's realized active return was -0.6pp, led by a -0.8pp public-equity selection effect [S4]. Governed ex ante attribution is +0.4pp on persisted one-year expected returns, with fixed-income selection the largest positive effect [S5]. Both lanes reconcile within their returned tolerance, but their realized linked and single-period expected bases are not interchangeable [S4][S5].

blocks.title: Basis difference
blocks.text: Historical effects use realized monthly observations and symmetric-Carino linking; ex ante effects use current normalized cohort weights and one expected period. The values are not directly interchangeable [S4][S5].

blocks.text: Public equity changes sign between the returned lanes, while fixed income and private assets retain their direction [S4][S5]. Historical effects are concentrated in public-equity selection; ex ante positive effects are shared by public equity and fixed income [S4][S5]. These observations describe returned sign and rank only.

blocks.title: Reconciliation diagnostics
rows: Assumption set and regime IDs are null [S5]

items: Historical effects cover 12 complete monthly observations and use returned symmetric-Carino linking [S4].
Ex ante effects use current actual and persisted policy benchmark weights normalized within the root sibling cohort [S5].
Persisted expected returns are in USD; currency effects are not separately included [S5].
Assumption-set and regime identities are not attached to the persisted expectations [S5].
Missing evidence would remain unavailable rather than being treated as zero.

blocks.title: Public-equity effect direction
blocks.text: Observation: public equity is -0.6pp historically and +0.3pp ex ante [S4][S5]. Why it matters: the sign change separates realized experience from current expectations. Uncertainty: the lanes use different periods and weight bases. Consideration for discussion: whether the persisted public-equity expectation still reflects the intended policy basis.

blocks.title: Selection concentration
blocks.text: Observation: historical selection is the largest total negative component [S4]. Why it matters: active return was concentrated in one effect type. Uncertainty: segment attribution does not by itself identify security or manager skill. Consideration for discussion: which underlying evidence would be needed to explain the returned selection effect.

blocks.title: Assumption lineage
blocks.text: Observation: the ex ante result has no linked assumption-set or regime identifier [S5]. Why it matters: the persisted inputs cannot be tied to a named release in this report. Uncertainty: input dates may differ by segment. Consideration for discussion: whether assumption lineage needs separate governance review.
